clue.text: Stand in where I put seed carelessly

indicators.note: seed sown carelessly lands in a jumble, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener admits to sowing seed haphazardly in some patch.
explanation.walkthrough: The feed dropped the 'I' that the printed page shows; with it, I plus PUT SEED gives exactly the eight letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To deputise is to act as a substitute for someone, which is what standing in means.

clue.text: The old fogey selling fake jewelry

explanation.definitionFit: A duffer is an incompetent old buffer, and in old slang a pedlar passing off sham goods as valuable.

clue.text: A playful reminder

parts.note: read as a reminder given during a play, to an actor who forgets a line

explanation.definitionFit: A prompter in the wings feeds a forgotten line to an actor during a play.

clue.text: They get the right notes with some difficulty

definitions.text: They get the right notes with some difficulty

indicators.note: the letters are got into order only with an effort, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: High male singers strain to reach the correct pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenors are high male voices who often strain for their top notes.

clue.text: Virginia's river of shanty fame?

parts.note: a river of the US state that names a famous sea song

explanation.definitionFit: The Shenandoah flows through Virginia and gives its name to a well-known sea shanty.

clue.text: Esoteric officer who commands worship

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for Officer Commanding
a cult is a system of religious worship or devotion

explanation.surface: A mysterious commander leads a body of devoted followers.
explanation.definitionFit: Occult knowledge is secret and reserved for initiates, as esoteric knowledge is.

clue.text: Noisy girl on the roundabout ?

parts.note: a Greek muse whose name also belongs to a loud steam organ heard at fairs

explanation.walkthrough: A roundabout is a British fairground merry-go-round; the steam organ that plays beside it shares its name with the muse of epic poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope, muse of epic poetry, gives her name to the loud steam organ of the fairground.

clue.text: The dianist seeks to be so modern

definitions.text: The dianist seeks to be so modern

parts.words: The dianist seeks to be so modern
parts.note: a diary keeper wants entries written right up to today's date

explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'dianist', a misprint for 'diarist': a diary keeper wants the entries to reach today's date.
explanation.definitionFit: Being current and modern is being abreast of the latest date.

clue.text: A poetic contribution to the Book of Lamentations?

definitions.text: A poetic contribution to the Book of Lamentations?

parts.words: A poetic contribution to the Book of Lamentations?
parts.note: a mourning song or poem, the kind of verse a book of laments would hold

explanation.definitionFit: A threnody is a song or poem of mourning, a lament for the dead.

clue.text: Struggle to get Miss Nightingale below?

parts.note: Florence Nightingale, the nursing pioneer, is shortened to Flo
below and under both mean beneath

explanation.surface: Someone strains to fetch the famous nurse from downstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounder is to thrash about or struggle clumsily.

clue.text: Overhead worker or abusive critic?

explanation.definitionFit: A roofer laying tiles works above our heads; one who slates a book or play attacks it harshly.

clue.text: The fiery heavens

parts.note: the highest sphere of the old cosmology, thought to be made of pure fire

explanation.definitionFit: In medieval cosmology the highest heaven was a realm of pure fire, the seat of God.

clue.text: Lea produces material without copper

indicators.note: here 'without' means outside, so the cloth wraps around the coin

parts.note: linen is a cloth woven from flax
a copper is a penny, and d is the old abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A meadow yields fabric that needs no copper in its making.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense outside, not lacking. The definition is loose: a lime tree is something a lea, or meadow, may produce.
explanation.definitionFit: The linden or lime is a tree that grows in open meadowland.

clue.text: Lambent, like those early films

explanation.definitionFit: Lambent light plays softly and wavers; early cinema films jumped and wavered, hence the nickname flicks.

clue.text: Got a bad head?

parts.note: read as the head, or pate, having gone off like a rotten egg

explanation.definitionFit: A muddled or stupid person is said to have a confused, scrambled brain.

clue.text: Source of artistic leaves

parts.note: the plant whose leaves painters and sculptors used to cover nudity

explanation.definitionFit: Fig leaves were the traditional covering for nude figures in painting and sculpture.

clue.text: Not quite up to the standard of Housman's cherry

definitions.text: Not quite up to the standard of Housman's cherry

parts.words: Not quite up to the standard of Housman's cherry
parts.note: the poet called the cherry the most beautiful of trees, so anything else is a degree short

explanation.definitionFit: Housman's poem opens 'Loveliest of trees, the cherry now', so one step short of the superlative is the comparative.

clue.text: Wild flower suggesting wealth for the farmer?

definitions.text: Wild flower suggesting wealth for the farmer?

parts.words: Wild flower suggesting wealth for the farmer?
parts.note: a plant whose name sounds like farm cash, agricultural plus money

explanation.definitionFit: Agrimony is a yellow-flowered plant of hedgerows and verges.

clue.text: A look from Chancellor Bismarck reveals the ore

parts.note: Otto von Bismarck was known as the Iron Chancellor
a glance is a quick look

explanation.surface: A stern stare from the German statesman tells you something.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron glance is an old name for haematite, a mineral from which iron is smelted.

clue.text: Air filter?

explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a tune or melody; to strain liquid is to pass it through a sieve.

clue.text: Unusually heartless singers

parts.note: the sea nymphs of myth whose songs lured sailors to their deaths

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these women sang sweetly to wreck passing ships without pity.

clue.text: Anything but pretty these Victorian bonnet trimmings

definitions.text: Anything but pretty these Victorian bonnet trimmings

parts.words: Anything but pretty these Victorian bonnet trimmings
parts.note: shades fitted to Victorian bonnets were named for being plain and unattractive

explanation.definitionFit: In the Victorian era an ugly was a silk shade worn over the front of a bonnet.

clue.text: It's the turn of the classical bathing belle

indicators.note: the two words swap places, so the second is put first

parts.note: taken as written
'tis is the old contraction of it is

explanation.surface: A swimming beauty from antiquity finally gets her moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn of' tells you to put 'the' before 'tis'. Thetis was a sea nymph in Greek myth, mother of Achilles, so she is a classical belle who lives in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Thetis was a Nereid, a sea nymph of Greek legend, so a classical bather.

clue.text: Look at it, it's boiling !

parts.note: to see something is to look at it
an unnamed it is a thing

explanation.surface: Someone points at a pot that has come to the boil.
explanation.definitionFit: Seething water is bubbling hard, as when it boils.

clue.text: The play is over for this returning inventor

indicators.note: returning means the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: in rugby the referee calls no side to end the match

explanation.surface: An inventor goes home once the show has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: NO SIDE is the rugby term for the end of a match; read backwards it gives EDISON, Thomas Edison, inventor of the phonograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison patented the phonograph, the electric light bulb and many other devices.

clue.text: Recorder of ancient Rome in Persia, oddly enough

indicators.note: said of something strange, so these letters are taken in a strange new order

explanation.surface: A historian of Rome is found, surprisingly, in Persia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like a signal to take odd letters, but here the letters of IN PERSIA are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Piranesi made celebrated etchings of the ruins of ancient Rome.

clue.text: It's light in the streets for wanderers

indicators.note: the beam is placed in the middle of the abbreviation

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, so streets are Sts
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Lamplight on the roads guides those who roam about at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Strays are lost or homeless animals that roam about.

clue.text: Contends in the arena, painfully, or in the adjoining columns?

definitions.text: Contends in the arena, painfully, or in the adjoining columns?

parts.words: Contends in the arena, painfully, or in the adjoining columns?
parts.note: struggling as a Greek athlete in the games, suffering pain, or a solver wrestling with this puzzle

explanation.definitionFit: The Greek agon was a contest; to agonise is to struggle or suffer, as a solver might over the clues.
